fields.rt-blog-html:
Imagine the tantalizing smell of spices wafting from your kitchen, the smiles of families gathered around your delicious halal dishes, and the satisfaction of bringing your community a place where food rhymes with sharing and respect for tradition. 

That's what the dream of opening a halal fast food restaurant sounds like. But where do you start? Follow the Innovorder guide now!

‍

The halal market

In France, with an estimated Muslim population of 5 million, the halal market is proving to be a buoyant sector for entrepreneurs and investors alike. This market, worth around 4.5 billion euros in the food sector and 1 billion euros in the out-of-home sector, particularly in the fast-food sector, demonstrates considerable growth potential.

The halal market penetration rate is estimated at 71%, underlining consumers' growing interest in these products. Foodservice, in particular, is undergoing remarkable expansion, offering numerous opportunities for the development of new offerings tailored to halal requirements. This positive dynamic indicates that the halal catering sector in France is becoming an even more significant segment of the national economy, with prospects for continued growth.

‍

Step 1: The business plan, your compass

Think of the business plan as a treasure map. This essential document doesn't just describe your business idea; it's the beating heart of it, the guide that will guide you every step of the way. Here's how to build it step by step:

Defining your vision

Start by putting down on paper what you're passionate about: why a halal fast food restaurant? What makes your concept unique? This vision will be the beacon that lights up your entire project.

Market analysis

Here, we get to the heart of the matter. Who are your future customers? What are their unmet needs? Examine the competition: who are they, what are their strengths and weaknesses? This analysis will help you position yourself strategically in the market.

Determining your offer

What are you going to put on the plate? Your menu should reflect your identity while meeting your customers' expectations. Make a list of your specialties, and don't forget to add that little "something extra" that will make all the difference.

Business model

How will you generate revenue? On-site sales, takeaway, delivery... the options are numerous. Determine your business model, making sure it's viable and profitable. This is also the time to set your price scale.

Marketing plan

How will you promote your restaurant? 

Social networks, local partnerships, promotional campaigns: your marketing plan needs to be both creative and pragmatic. It needs to reflect your brand identity while attracting customers.

Budget forecast

This is one of the most technical aspects, but one that is of the utmost importance. 

How much will it cost to open your restaurant? How much do you need to sell to be profitable? This budget forecast will include your initial investments, your fixed and variable costs, and your sales forecasts.

To find out more: How to balance your restaurant budget

Planning

Last but not least: when and how are you going to implement all this? Define a realistic timetable for your project, from administrative procedures to opening.

Building a solid business plan takes time and thought, but it's an invaluable investment in the success of your project. Not only will it help you clarify your ideas, it will also help you convince partners and financial backers to join you in this adventure.

👉 To find out more: 4 steps to opening a fast-food restaurant

‍

‍

Step 2: The importance of halal standards and certification

Obtaining halal certification is essential to guarantee that your offer meets consumer expectations.

Halal certification is not just a label, it's a promise of quality and respect for your customers. It's essential to understand the different certifications available and the steps involved in obtaining them. It proves your commitment and strengthens the trust of your customers.

Here is a list of 12 certification bodies:

  • SFCVH
  • ACMIF
  • ARGML
  • ACHAHADA
  • EUROPEAN HALAL SERVICE
  • ARRISSALA
  • AGRML
  • ACHAHADA
  • ALTAKWA
  • ARRISSALA
  • MUSLIM CONSEIL INTERNATIONAL
  • HALAL SERVICE

‍

Step 3: A concept that suits you

Your restaurant should reflect your passion and vision. Traditional halal fast food or innovative culinary fusion, the choice is yours. 

The important thing is to create a space where people feel good, a place that invites the senses to travel, while remaining rooted in halal traditions.

Clearly defining your concept is essential, whether it's a traditional halal fast-food restaurant (burgers, pizzas, tacos) or a more elaborate concept (Asian, Indian, Lebanese cuisine).

‍

Step 4: Financing your dream

Let's talk about money. Between personal contributions, bank loans and possible grants, you have several options for financing your project. 

Now is the time to fine-tune your financial plan and convince your bankers that your project is rock-solid!

👉 To find out more: Creating a restaurant: how to finance your project?

‍

Step 5: Location, a strategic decision

The choice of location is crucial. Good visibility, easy access and an understanding of the local fabric are major assets. Do your research and take the time to find the ideal location for your dream.

👉 To find out more: How to find the perfect premises for your restaurant

‍

Step 6: Human and material resources, the keys to success

Your team will be the beating heart of your restaurant. Recruiting people who share your values and investing in their training, particularly in halal standards, is essential. 

When it comes to equipment, don't skimp on quality. Your kitchen is your workshop, and it must be equipped to meet your ambitions.

‍

Step 7: Get the word out about your restaurant

Good marketing works wonders. In addition to a solid online presence (website, social networks), think of original launch strategies to create buzz. 

Special offers, collaborations with local influencers, anything to draw attention to your new restaurant.
